title: Not Built For This #6: Maximum Temperature

sentences.en: This is episode 6 of Not Built for This, Maximum Temperature.
sentences.zh: 这是《不适宜居住》系列的第六集，主题是“最高气温”。

sentences.en: Last summer, temperatures in Phoenix, Arizona got above 110 degrees for more than 30 days in a row.
sentences.zh: 去年夏天，亚利桑那州凤凰城的气温连续超过30天达到110华氏度（约43摄氏度）以上。

sentences.en: A couple of times in July, the thermometer nearly cracked 120.
sentences.zh: 七月里有几次，温度计几乎要冲破120华氏度（约49摄氏度）。

sentences.en: It is always hot in Phoenix in the summertime, but this was a new and unwelcome record.
sentences.zh: 凤凰城的夏天总是很热，但这创下了一个前所未有的、令人不安的纪录。

sentences.en: And as the city endured this string of unbearably hot days, there was this one image that I became fixated on.
sentences.zh: 当这座城市忍受着这一连串酷热难耐的日子时，有一个画面让我久久无法忘怀。

sentences.en: All right, check this out.
sentences.zh: 好了，看看这个。

sentences.en: Even the saguaros here in the valley can't take the heat anymore.
sentences.zh: 就连山谷里的巨人柱仙人掌也受不了这种高温了。

sentences.en: It's become a summer trend that just won't seem to stop.
sentences.zh: 这已经成为一种似乎停不下来的夏季趋势。

sentences.en: Our beloved saguaros toppling to the ground and it's leaving many neighbors...
sentences.zh: 我们心爱的巨人柱仙人掌纷纷倒地，这让许多居民……

sentences.en: All across the city, saguaros were keeling over in the heat.
sentences.zh: 全城各地的巨人柱仙人掌都在高温下倾倒。

sentences.en: But these massive, stately cacti can grow up to 60 feet tall and weigh thousands of pounds.
sentences.zh: 但这些高大庄严的仙人掌可以长到60英尺（约18米）高，重达数千磅。

sentences.en: And they were coming down left and right, crushing cars and denting roofs.
sentences.zh: 它们接二连三地倒下，砸坏了汽车，压瘪了屋顶。

sentences.en: I just started hearing a loud crack.
sentences.zh: 我刚开始听到一声巨响。

sentences.en: So I looked up and I just saw the cactus falling over.
sentences.zh: 所以我抬头看，就看见仙人掌倒了下来。

sentences.en: A good amount of the roof, like the drywall, fell off.
sentences.zh: 很大一部分屋顶，比如干墙，都塌了。

sentences.en: Our next-door neighbors thought it was like a minor earthquake.
sentences.zh: 我们的邻居还以为是发生了小地震。

sentences.en: The saguaro is a master of desert survival.
sentences.zh: 巨人柱仙人掌是沙漠生存的大师。

sentences.en: There's literally nothing about its physical being, from its waxy skin to its spongy interiors,
sentences.zh: 从它那蜡质的表皮到海绵状的内部，它的身体构造中，

sentences.en: that isn't adapted to Arizona's furnace-blast temperatures.
sentences.zh: 几乎没有哪一部分不是为了适应亚利桑那州火炉般的高温而进化的。

sentences.en: And yet, here they were, dying.
sentences.zh: 然而，它们现在却在死去。

sentences.en: Well, I thought it would outlive me by 100 years.
sentences.zh: 我原以为它能比我多活100年。

sentences.en: It seemed like a pretty ominous sign.
sentences.zh: 这看起来是一个相当不祥的征兆。

sentences.en: If the saguaros couldn't survive in the heat, what did it mean for us?
sentences.zh: 如果连巨人柱仙人掌都无法在高温中生存，那对我们来说意味着什么？

sentences.en: I first got interested in heat in Phoenix.
sentences.zh: 我最初对高温产生兴趣是在凤凰城。

sentences.en: I had been covering climate change for 20 years and didn't give heat much thought, as strange as that may seem.
sentences.zh: 我报道气候变化已经20年了，却没怎么考虑过高温问题，尽管这听起来很奇怪。

sentences.en: This is the climate writer Jeff Goodell.
sentences.zh: 这位是气候作家杰夫·古德尔。

sentences.en: He's the author of the book The Heat Will Kill You FirSt.
sentences.zh: 他是《高温将首先杀死你》一书的作者。

sentences.en: And he got interested in heat when he was in downtown Phoenix in the middle of summer
sentences.zh: 他是在盛夏时节身处凤凰城市中心时对高温产生兴趣的，

sentences.en: and decided to walk 20 blocks to a median.
sentences.zh: 当时他决定步行20个街区去一个路中间的隔离带。

sentences.en: Rookie move.
sentences.zh: 真是新手操作。

sentences.en: I mean, it was like walking into a kind of solid wall of this invisible force
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那感觉就像走进了一堵由某种无形力量构成的坚硬墙壁，

sentences.en: that just surrounds you and envelops you and kind of suffocates you
sentences.zh: 它包围着你、笼罩着你，让你感到窒息，

sentences.en: and makes your body, I mean, the only word I can use to kind of describe it is freak out.
sentences.zh: 让你的身体……我只能用“抓狂”这个词来形容那种感觉。

sentences.en: And by the time I got to my meeting, I was dizzy, my heart was pounding, and I was a little off balance.
sentences.zh: 等我赶到开会地点时，我已经头晕目眩，心跳加速，身体有些失衡。

sentences.en: And I realized, oh my gosh, heat is dangerous.
sentences.zh: 我意识到，天哪，高温是危险的。

sentences.en: If I had to go another 20 blocks, I don't know if I would make it.
sentences.zh: 如果我还要再走20个街区，我不知道自己还能不能撑住。

sentences.en: So for me, that was the beginning of everything.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，那是这一切的开始。

sentences.en: Specifically, the beginning of Jeff trying to understand what climate change will mean for us on a physiological level.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，是杰夫开始尝试从生理层面理解气候变化对我们意味着什么的开始。

sentences.en: The impacts of climate disasters are often assessed in terms of property damage.
sentences.zh: 气候灾难的影响通常是根据财产损失来评估的。

sentences.en: When a hurricane hits a place like Florida, the news shows images of gas stations ripped open like tin cans,
sentences.zh: 当飓风袭击佛罗里达等地时，新闻画面显示加油站像易拉罐一样被撕开，

sentences.en: homes flattened by the wind, cars floating down a flooded main street.
sentences.zh: 房屋被风夷为平地，汽车在被淹的主干道上漂浮。

sentences.en: We talk about the millions of dollars of damage.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是数百万美元的损失。

sentences.en: But in places like Phoenix and in hot places all over the world,
sentences.zh: 但在凤凰城和世界各地炎热的地方，

sentences.en: climate change is wreaking a very different kind of havoc on living things, on people's bodies.
sentences.zh: 气候变化正在对生物、对人们的身体造成一种截然不同的破坏。

sentences.en: Heat kills more people every year than any other weather event.
sentences.zh: 每年因高温死亡的人数比任何其他天气事件都要多。

sentences.en: The best estimate on the annual death toll is around 500,000 people globally.
sentences.zh: 据估计，全球每年因高温死亡的人数约为50万人。

sentences.en: But that's almost certainly an undercount.
sentences.zh: 但这几乎肯定是被低估了。

sentences.en: And yet, even as we're freaking out about our warming world,
sentences.zh: 然而，即使我们对变暖的世界感到恐慌，

sentences.en: many of us still don't really think about heat itself as an existential threat.
sentences.zh: 我们中的许多人仍然没有真正把高温本身视为一种生存威胁。

sentences.en: And I think that's at least in part because of the language that we used for many years to describe this crisis.
sentences.zh: 我认为这至少部分是因为我们多年来描述这场危机所使用的语言。

sentences.en: The phrase global warming does not sound very alarming.
sentences.zh: “全球变暖”这个词听起来并不怎么令人担忧。

sentences.en: It sounds like maybe we should get our beach chairs and go to the beach.
sentences.zh: 听起来好像我们应该带上沙滩椅去海边度假一样。

sentences.en: It sounds like time for shorts and flip-flops.
sentences.zh: 听起来像是该穿短裤和人字拖的时候了。

sentences.en: In other words, if our global temperatures increase by, say, a few degrees,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果全球气温上升，比如说几度，

sentences.en: is that really something to get all bent out of shape about?
sentences.zh: 那真的值得大惊小怪吗？

sentences.en: No, it doesn't sound dangerous at all.
sentences.zh: 不，这听起来一点也不危险。

sentences.en: It just sounds like, you know, I have other bigger problems to worry about
sentences.zh: 听起来就像是，你知道，我有其他更重要的问题要担心，

sentences.en: than whether it's 78 or 80 degrees outside.
sentences.zh: 而不是外面是78度还是80度。

sentences.en: But a few degrees do matter.
sentences.zh: 但几度确实很重要。

sentences.en: Last year, 2023, was the hottest year ever recorded in human history.
sentences.zh: 去年，即2023年，是有记录以来人类历史上最热的一年。

sentences.en: The last time the world was this hot was 125,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 上一次世界如此炎热是在12.5万年前。

sentences.en: And as we build on a hotter baseline, heat waves also get more extreme and more deadly.
sentences.zh: 随着我们在更高的基准温度上继续升温，热浪也变得更加极端、更加致命。

sentences.en: Phoenix, Arizona has the dubious distinction of being the hottest major city in America.
sentences.zh: 亚利桑那州凤凰城有着“美国最热大城市”这一令人尴尬的称号。

sentences.en: And it's perhaps the best place in the country to investigate our confused relationship with heat and its effects on our health.
sentences.zh: 它或许是全国调查我们与高温之间混乱关系及其对健康影响的最佳地点。

sentences.en: It's a place that's marketed itself as a warm and pleasant escape from the snowbound north.
sentences.zh: 这个地方一直将自己营销为逃离北方冰雪的温暖宜人之地。

sentences.en: But now there are people in the Valley of the Sun looking at these warming trends, and they're worried.
sentences.zh: 但现在，太阳谷的居民们看着这些变暖趋势，感到忧心忡忡。

sentences.en: As Phoenix continues to grow, with thousands of new residents arriving every year,
sentences.zh: 随着凤凰城持续扩张，每年有成千上万的新居民涌入，

sentences.en: there are advocates pushing the city and even the federal government to recognize extreme heat for what it is,
sentences.zh: 有倡导者推动市政府乃至联邦政府去正视极端高温的本质，

sentences.en: a force that is testing our biological limits.
sentences.zh: 即一种正在考验我们生物极限的力量。

sentences.en: Because our bodies were not built for this.
sentences.zh: 因为我们的身体并非为此而生。

sentences.en: This is the final episode in our series.
sentences.zh: 这是我们系列的最后一集。

sentences.en: I'm Emmett Fitzgerald.
sentences.zh: 我是埃米特·菲茨杰拉德。

sentences.en: 99PI senior editor Delaney Hall is also our in-house desert correspondent.
sentences.zh: 99PI的高级编辑德莱尼·霍尔也是我们的驻地沙漠通讯员。

sentences.en: She lives in New Mexico.
sentences.zh: 她住在新墨西哥州。

sentences.en: And last year, she made a trip to Phoenix to try and understand how heat went from being
sentences.zh: 去年，她前往凤凰城，试图了解高温是如何从

sentences.en: the city's number one selling point to a public health crisis.
sentences.zh: 这座城市最大的卖点变成一场公共卫生危机的。

sentences.en: Last summer, on a 100-degree day, I went out driving around Phoenix with a guy named Sergio Armandadiz.
sentences.zh: 去年夏天，在气温达到100华氏度（约38摄氏度）的一天，我开车带着一个叫塞尔吉奥·阿曼达迪兹的人在凤凰城转悠。

sentences.en: So are we going to some Circle Ks?
sentences.zh: 我们要去几家Circle K便利店吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, we have a list here of store addresses.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们这里有一份商店地址清单。

sentences.en: I'll check in with the manager, and I'll let him know that I'm here doing outreach.
sentences.zh: 我会去和经理打个招呼，告诉他我在这里做外展服务。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Sergio does street outreach with the Phoenix Rescue Mission.
sentences.zh: 塞尔吉奥在凤凰城救援中心从事街头外展工作。

sentences.en: It's an organization that works with homeless people in Phoenix.
sentences.zh: 这是一个致力于帮助凤凰城无家可归者的组织。

sentences.en: And today, I'm tagging along with him while he hits up a number of convenience stores.
sentences.zh: 今天，我跟着他走访了多家便利店。

sentences.en: And is there a reason people kind of tend to group around the Circle Ks?
sentences.zh: 人们倾向于聚集在Circle K便利店周围是有原因的吗？

sentences.en: Like, what's going on there from a homeless person's perspective?
sentences.zh: 从无家可归者的角度来看，那里发生了什么？

sentences.en: You know, on a hot day, you can grab a bunch of ice and grab some soda.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在炎热的天气里，你可以弄到很多冰块和汽水。

sentences.en: You know, it's pretty cheap.
sentences.zh: 而且价格很便宜。

sentences.en: Polar Pops was my favorite thing.
sentences.zh: Polar Pops（冷饮）是我最喜欢的东西。

sentences.en: So, if you got food stamps, you can go get some quick food real quick, you know?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你有食品券，你可以很快买到一些快餐，你知道吗？

sentences.en: It's like turning into a Circle K advertisement.
sentences.zh: 这听起来快变成Circle K的广告了。

sentences.en: The city of Phoenix is trying all sorts of ways to make itself cooler as the planet heats up.
sentences.zh: 随着地球变暖，凤凰城市政府正在尝试各种方法来让自己降温。

sentences.en: They're painting streets with reflective coating to repel the sun.
sentences.zh: 他们正在街道上涂抹反光涂层以反射阳光。

sentences.en: They're planting lots of trees.
sentences.zh: 他们正在种植大量的树木。

sentences.en: And they're building out a network of cooling centers where people can go hang out during the heat of the day.
sentences.zh: 他们正在建立一个降温中心网络，人们可以在白天最热的时候去那里休息。

sentences.en: They've even got a new heat czar, whose job is to help cool the city down.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至任命了一位新的“高温沙皇”，其职责就是帮助城市降温。

sentences.en: But when it comes to saving lives, during the hottest summer in history, at least the hottest one so far,
sentences.zh: 但在历史上最热的夏天——至少是迄今为止最热的一个夏天——谈到拯救生命时，

sentences.en: it's hard to imagine anyone with a more important job than Sergio.
sentences.zh: 很难想象还有谁的工作比塞尔吉奥更重要。

sentences.en: We're going to go get some ice.
sentences.zh: 我们要去弄点冰块。

sentences.en: I think it's important that I have some cold water.
sentences.zh: 我觉得随身带点凉水很重要。

sentences.en: It's a good icebreaker.
sentences.zh: 这是个很好的破冰方式。

sentences.en: No pun intended.
sentences.zh: 没有双关的意思。

sentences.en: Sergio is a remarkably chill guy.
sentences.zh: 塞尔吉奥是个非常冷静的人。

sentences.en: He drives all over the city, cranking the A.C., cracking jokes, and talking about Jesus.
sentences.zh: 他开着车在城市里到处跑，开着空调，开着玩笑，谈论着耶稣。

sentences.en: But his work also has high stakes.
sentences.zh: 但他的工作也面临着巨大的风险。

sentences.en: Every summer, hundreds of people in Phoenix die from the heat.
sentences.zh: 每年夏天，凤凰城都有数百人死于高温。

sentences.en: And many of them are homeless.
sentences.zh: 其中许多人是无家可归者。

sentences.en: Sergio knows firsthand how hard it can be to survive when you have nowhere to go to escape the heat.
sentences.zh: 塞尔吉奥亲身体会过，当你无处躲避高温时，生存是多么艰难。

sentences.en: I've slept at this park before.
sentences.zh: 我以前在这个公园睡过觉。

sentences.en: He did it himself for five years.
sentences.zh: 他自己曾经历过五年的流浪生活。

sentences.en: My stomping grounds weren't too far from here.
sentences.zh: 我以前的地盘离这儿不远。

sentences.en: And now he works in a lot of the same neighborhoods where he once camped or hung out or spent hours looking for scraps of shade.
sentences.zh: 现在，他在许多曾经露宿、闲逛或花数小时寻找阴凉处的地方工作。

sentences.en: When we pull up at the Circle K, there are a couple people hanging out at the side of the store.
sentences.zh: 当我们把车停在Circle K时，有几个人在商店旁边闲逛。

sentences.en: Sergio approaches a man to see about getting him into a shelter for the night, while I sit and talk with a middle-aged woman.
sentences.zh: 塞尔吉奥走近一名男子，看能否让他当晚住进收容所，而我则坐下来与一位中年妇女交谈。

sentences.en: She has a repurposed baby stroller packed full of her stuff, including a cute, scruffy little dog.
sentences.zh: 她推着一辆改装过的婴儿车，里面塞满了她的东西，还有一只可爱、毛茸茸的小狗。

sentences.en: What's that little guy's name?
sentences.zh: 那个小家伙叫什么名字？

sentences.en: That's Chupacabra.
sentences.zh: 它叫卓柏卡布拉。

sentences.en: Chupacabra.
sentences.zh: 卓柏卡布拉。

sentences.en: Hey, he goes nuts when he sees another dog.
sentences.zh: 嘿，它一看到别的狗就发疯。

sentences.en: This is Bunny.
sentences.zh: 这是邦妮。

sentences.en: She came to Phoenix in 1986 and then says that she got stuck.
sentences.zh: 她1986年来到凤凰城，然后说她就困在这里了。

sentences.en: She's been living here for almost 40 years, homeless on and off.
sentences.zh: 她在这里住了快40年了，断断续续地过着无家可归的生活。

sentences.en: And so by now, she's developed a lot of tricks for beating the heat.
sentences.zh: 所以到现在，她已经总结出了一套对抗高温的秘诀。

sentences.en: She carries an umbrella.
sentences.zh: 她随身带着一把伞。

sentences.en: She wears a rag dipped in cold water around her neck.
sentences.zh: 她脖子上围着一块浸过冷水的破布。

sentences.en: And she makes sure she stays hydrated.
sentences.zh: 而且她确保自己保持水分充足。

sentences.en: You know, all we can do is try to find a shady spot to sit if the cops don't run us out.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果警察不赶我们走，我们能做的就是找个阴凉的地方坐着。

sentences.en: Most times we're stuck out in the sun.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候我们只能待在太阳底下。

sentences.en: And it really sucks.
sentences.zh: 那感觉真的很糟糕。

sentences.en: Because there's nowhere out there to really cool down.
sentences.zh: 因为外面根本没有地方可以真正降温。

sentences.en: It's hot, nasty, muggy, dirty, filthy.
sentences.zh: 又热、又恶心、又闷、又脏、又邋遢。

sentences.en: Just all around bad news.
sentences.zh: 总之就是各种糟糕。

sentences.en: You know, I feel like Arizona has this thing where people come because they love the sun
sentences.zh: 你知道，我觉得亚利桑那州有一种魔力，人们来这里是因为他们热爱阳光，

sentences.en: and they love the life here.
sentences.zh: 热爱这里的生活。

sentences.en: Have you found that?
sentences.zh: 你发现了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I've found a few people that like it, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，我确实遇到过一些喜欢这里的人。

sentences.en: But there's very few of them that like it whenever it hits 120, 125.
sentences.zh: 但当气温达到120、125华氏度时，没几个人会喜欢它。

sentences.en: Then they want to scurry inside where their air conditioning is, you know?
sentences.zh: 那时候他们就想躲进有空调的室内，你知道吗？

sentences.en: We're out here 24-7.
sentences.zh: 我们却得24小时待在外面。

sentences.en: They get to go home in their nice, comfortable air conditioners.
sentences.zh: 他们可以回到舒适的空调房里。

sentences.en: Bunny has hit on a central fact about life in modern Phoenix,
sentences.zh: 邦妮道出了现代凤凰城生活的一个核心事实，

sentences.en: which is that the heat affects people in profoundly unequal ways.
sentences.zh: 那就是高温对人们的影响存在着极大的不平等。

sentences.en: For some, it's an asset.
sentences.zh: 对一些人来说，它是资产。

sentences.en: For others, it's a liability.
sentences.zh: 对另一些人来说，它是负担。

sentences.en: And this inequity goes back a long way in Phoenix's history.
sentences.zh: 这种不平等在凤凰城的历史上由来已久。

sentences.en: Nearly 1,000 years ago,
indigenous people found ways to live with the heat of the Sonoran Desert.
sentences.zh: 原住民就找到了与索诺兰沙漠高温共存的方法。

sentences.en: They created cliff dwellings where the temperatures were cooler.
sentences.zh: 他们建造了气温较低的悬崖居所。

sentences.en: They built homes with thick walls of stone and mud.
sentences.zh: 他们用厚厚的石头和泥土建造房屋。

sentences.en: And for centuries, the population of central Arizona stayed relatively small.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，亚利桑那州中部的人口一直保持在相对较小的规模。

sentences.en: The extreme heat provided a check on development,
sentences.zh: 极端的高温曾一度限制了城市的发展，

sentences.en: and Phoenix remained a sleepy outpoSt.
sentences.zh: 而菲尼克斯依然是一个沉睡的边陲小镇。

sentences.en: But fast forward to the 1950s and 60s, and that began to change.
sentences.zh: 但快进到20世纪50和60年代，情况开始发生变化。

sentences.en: City boosters began selling Phoenix precisely because of its climate.
sentences.zh: 城市推广者们开始以气候为卖点来推销菲尼克斯。

sentences.en: They pitched it as a land without winter, where you could play golf year-round.
sentences.zh: 他们将其宣传为一片没有冬天的土地，在那里你可以全年打高尔夫球。

sentences.en: And it turned out that hundreds of thousands of people wanted in on that vision.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，成千上万的人都向往这种愿景。

sentences.en: And if it got a little toasty in the summertime,
sentences.zh: 如果夏天变得有点闷热，

sentences.en: there was a newfangled technology that could help you with that.
sentences.zh: 还有一种新奇的技术可以帮你解决这个问题。

sentences.en: So, you can find people in the early 60s talking about living, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，在60年代早期，你可以听到人们谈论着，你知道，

sentences.en: completely air-conditioned lives.
sentences.zh: 过着完全空调化的生活。

sentences.en: This is Andrew Needham, a historian who studies the environmental
sentences.zh: 这位是安德鲁·尼达姆，一位研究美国西部环境

sentences.en: and indigenous history of the American WeSt.
sentences.zh: 和原住民历史的历史学家。

sentences.en: And Andrew told me about this old article he found in the Saturday Evening PoSt.
sentences.zh: 安德鲁告诉了我他在《周六晚邮报》上发现的一篇旧文章。

sentences.en: It included an interview with a local banker.
sentences.zh: 里面包含了一位当地银行家的采访。

sentences.en: He boasted about how he got through the summer days.
sentences.zh: 他吹嘘自己是如何度过夏日的。

sentences.en: And he says, well, I wake up in my air-conditioned room.
sentences.zh: 他说，嗯，我在空调房里醒来。

sentences.en: I get in my air-conditioned car.
sentences.zh: 我坐进空调车里。

sentences.en: I go to the air-conditioned garage of my building.
sentences.zh: 我走进大楼的空调车库。

sentences.en: I go to my air-conditioned office.
sentences.zh: 我走进我的空调办公室。

sentences.en: At night, I go to an air-conditioned restaurant.
sentences.zh: 晚上，我去一家空调餐厅。

sentences.en: Maybe I see a movie in an air-conditioned theater.
sentences.zh: 也许我会在空调影院看场电影。

sentences.en: And so, you know, this kind of life entirely encased in the summer
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这种在夏天完全被包裹在

sentences.en: in refrigerated air conditioning is a reality for people like bankers.
sentences.zh: 冷气空调里的生活，对银行家这类人来说是现实。

sentences.en: But while bankers were bathing in this mechanically cooled air,
sentences.zh: 但当银行家们沐浴在这些机械冷却的空气中时，

sentences.en: working-class people in Phoenix were living much hotter lives.
sentences.zh: 菲尼克斯的工薪阶层却过着更加炎热的生活。

sentences.en: Back in the 1960s, the city was starkly divided by race and class and by temperature.
sentences.zh: 回到60年代，这座城市在种族、阶级和温度上有着鲜明的鸿沟。

sentences.en: When a reporter from the New Republic went to Phoenix to write about the city…
sentences.zh: 当《新共和》杂志的一位记者来到菲尼克斯报道这座城市时……

sentences.en: He says something to the effect of two cities stare at each other from opposite sides of a golf course,
sentences.zh: 他说大意是两座城市隔着高尔夫球场遥遥相望，

sentences.en: essentially saying that, like, here's this landscape of quality of life
sentences.zh: 本质上是说，这里存在着一种生活质量的景观，

sentences.en: in which African-American, Latino people have all been concentrated
sentences.zh: 非裔美国人和拉丁裔民众都被集中在

sentences.en: in kind of deteriorating and dilapidated housing.
sentences.zh: 那种破败不堪的住房里。

sentences.en: That inferior housing had flimsier insulation and older electrical systems,
sentences.zh: 那些劣质住房的隔热层更薄，电力系统也更老旧，

sentences.en: which made it harder to cool.
sentences.zh: 这使得降温变得更加困难。

sentences.en: And poorer neighborhoods typically had more concrete, fewer trees, and denser development,
sentences.zh: 贫困社区通常有更多的混凝土、更少的树木，开发也更密集，

sentences.en: all of which made the outdoor temperatures as much as 10 degrees hotter
sentences.zh: 所有这些都使得室外温度比城市中较富裕的地区

sentences.en: than in the wealthier parts of the city.
sentences.zh: 高出多达10度。

sentences.en: Even as access to A.C.
sentences.zh: 即使空调的普及率

sentences.en: has expanded,
sentences.zh: 有所提高，

sentences.en: poor people just have a harder time escaping the heat.
sentences.zh: 穷人依然更难逃避酷暑。

sentences.en: That was true decades ago, and it's still true today.
sentences.zh: 几十年前如此，今天依然如此。

sentences.en: Air conditioning is now nearly ubiquitous in Phoenix.
sentences.zh: 空调现在在菲尼克斯几乎无处不在。

sentences.en: Today, the vast majority of the city's buildings have A.C.
sentences.zh: 如今，该市绝大多数建筑都有空调。

sentences.en: But paradoxically, the fact that it's everywhere also makes the city vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 但矛盾的是，空调的普及也让这座城市变得脆弱。

sentences.en: That's because most builders today don't build with heat in mind.
sentences.zh: 这是因为如今大多数建筑商在建造时并不考虑防暑。

sentences.en: You know, we've forgotten…
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们已经忘记了……

sentences.en: Again, Jeff Goodell.
sentences.zh: 再次提到杰夫·古德尔。

sentences.en: …how to build buildings with natural ventilation.
sentences.zh: ……如何建造具有自然通风的建筑。

sentences.en: We've become dependent upon this machine, this cooling machine.
sentences.zh: 我们已经变得依赖这种机器，这种冷却机器。

sentences.en: Cooling modern buildings requires an enormous amount of electricity.
sentences.zh: 冷却现代建筑需要消耗巨大的电力。

sentences.en: And in a lot of places, including Phoenix, that energy still comes from fossil fuels.
sentences.zh: 而在许多地方，包括菲尼克斯，这些能源仍然来自化石燃料。

sentences.en: I didn't realize it, but air conditioning is responsible for about 4% of emissions globally,
sentences.zh: 我之前没意识到，空调在全球排放中约占4%，

sentences.en: which is nearly double the amount from the entire airline industry.
sentences.zh: 这几乎是整个航空业排放量的两倍。

sentences.en: And that means that while we're cooling ourselves off, we're also making ourselves hotter.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我们在给自己降温的同时，也在让地球变得更热。

sentences.en: So you get into this sort of perpetuating cycle of more air conditioning,
sentences.zh: 所以你陷入了一种恶性循环：更多的空调，

sentences.en: more burning of fossil fuels, and a hotter planet.
sentences.zh: 更多的化石燃料燃烧，以及一个更热的地球。

sentences.en: And that vicious cycle can become deadly.
sentences.zh: 而这种恶性循环可能会变得致命。

sentences.en: Because during an unprecedented heat wave, people crank the A.C.
sentences.zh: 因为在史无前例的热浪中，人们会把空调开到

sentences.en: as high as it can go,
sentences.zh: 最大功率，

sentences.en: which puts a lot of stress on the electrical grid
sentences.zh: 这给电网带来了巨大的压力，

sentences.en: and creates the potential for a catastrophic failure.
sentences.zh: 并造成了灾难性故障的可能。

sentences.en: It's like a sort of Damocles on a hotter planet.
sentences.zh: 这就像在变热的地球上悬着一把达摩克利斯之剑。

sentences.en: Air conditioning is great as long as it works.
sentences.zh: 空调只要能用就很好。

sentences.en: But if it fails, then we're all in big trouble.
sentences.zh: 但如果它坏了，那我们都有大麻烦了。

sentences.en: When we come back, the worst-case scenario.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我们将讨论最坏的情况。

sentences.en: In Phoenix, air conditioning has become a fact of life.
sentences.zh: 在菲尼克斯，空调已成为生活的一部分。

sentences.en: But what if the A.C.
sentences.zh: 但如果空调

sentences.en: fails?
sentences.zh: 坏了呢？

sentences.en: This is the kind of scenario that keeps emergency planners up at night.
sentences.zh: 这正是让应急规划者们彻夜难眠的情景。

sentences.en: And recently, a study came out that provided them with ample nightmare fuel.
sentences.zh: 最近，一项研究出炉，为他们提供了充足的噩梦素材。

sentences.en: The study modeled what would happen if a heat wave in Phoenix coincided with a grid failure,
sentences.zh: 该研究模拟了如果菲尼克斯的热浪与电网故障同时发生，

sentences.en: and then a multi-day blackout.
sentences.zh: 并导致持续数天的停电会发生什么。

sentences.en: The results were like the source material for a new Mad Max movie.
sentences.zh: 结果简直就像新版《疯狂的麦克斯》电影的素材。

sentences.en: The study predicted that half the city's population, nearly 800,000 people, would need emergency room care.
sentences.zh: 研究预测，全市一半的人口，近80万人，将需要急诊护理。

sentences.en: The city only has 3,000 emergency department beds.
sentences.zh: 而该市只有3000张急诊床位。

sentences.en: The study also showed that almost 13,000 people in Phoenix would die.
sentences.zh: 研究还显示，菲尼克斯将有近13000人死亡。

sentences.en: All of us were kind of like, my goodness, well, this would be not ideal.
sentences.zh: 我们当时都觉得，天哪，这可真是不妙。

sentences.en: This is Dr. Jeffrey Komp.
sentences.zh: 这位是杰弗里·康普医生。

sentences.en: He's an ER doctor at Valleywise Health, which serves Maricopa County.
sentences.zh: 他是服务于马里科帕县的Valleywise Health医院的急诊医生。

sentences.en: And I bet when he went to medical school, he didn't think he'd be doing work on the front lines of climate change.
sentences.zh: 我敢说，当他上医学院时，没想过自己会站在气候变化的最前线工作。

sentences.en: But much like Sergio, that's exactly what he's doing.
sentences.zh: 但就像塞尔吉奥一样，这正是他正在做的事情。

sentences.en: Every summer, Dr. Komp treats people coming into the ER with heat stroke.
sentences.zh: 每年夏天，康普医生都会救治因中暑被送进急诊室的患者。

sentences.en: People even get contact burns from touching the metal side of a car or falling down on a hot sidewalk.
sentences.zh: 人们甚至会因为触碰汽车金属侧面或摔倒在滚烫的人行道上而造成接触性烧伤。

sentences.en: But the summer of 2023 was different and maybe a sign of summers to come.
sentences.zh: 但2023年的夏天有所不同，这或许是未来夏天的预兆。

sentences.en: It's been really hot.
sentences.zh: 真的非常热。

sentences.en: It's been really, really hot.
sentences.zh: 真的，真的非常热。

sentences.en: And when we look at markers like mortality, so how many people die, it's much worse than last year.
sentences.zh: 当我们观察死亡率等指标时，也就是有多少人死亡，情况比去年糟糕得多。

sentences.en: I spoke with Dr. Komp towards the end of last summer.
sentences.zh: 我在去年夏天结束时采访了康普医生。

sentences.en: And deaths were up 52% from the previous year.
sentences.zh: 死亡人数比前一年增加了52%。

sentences.en: An estimated 645 people died from the heat in 2023.
sentences.zh: 据估计，2023年有645人死于高温。

sentences.en: And almost 300 of them were unhoused.
sentences.zh: 其中近300人是无家可归者。

sentences.en: Dr. Komp says people were arriving at the ER in truly mind-boggling conditions.
sentences.zh: 康普医生说，人们被送进急诊室时的状况简直令人难以置信。

sentences.en: Our thermometers top out at 109.
sentences.zh: 我们的体温计最高只能测到109度。

sentences.en: And personally, I've had multiple patients that have come in that have maxed out our thermometers.
sentences.zh: 我个人已经接诊过好几位患者，他们的体温都超出了体温计的上限。

sentences.en: So I honestly don't know what my, we call it T max or maximum temperature, has been for patients.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的不知道我的——我们称之为T-max或最高体温——患者的体温到底是多少。

sentences.en: But we've had people that come in incredibly, incredibly, incredibly hot.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实接诊过体温高得离谱的患者。

sentences.en: There are a couple different types of heat illness.
sentences.zh: 热相关疾病有几种不同的类型。

sentences.en: The first is what's known as classic heat stroke, which happens when you're exposed to heat for a prolonged time.
sentences.zh: 第一种是所谓的热射病，发生在你长时间暴露在高温下时。

sentences.en: This kind of heat stroke tends to affect the more vulnerable of us, like babies and older folks,
sentences.zh: 这种热射病往往影响我们中较脆弱的群体，比如婴儿和老年人，

sentences.en: pregnant people and people with chronic heart conditions and hypertension.
sentences.zh: 孕妇以及患有慢性心脏病和高血压的人。

sentences.en: The second kind is called exertional heat stroke, and it can happen to really anybody, even very healthy people, when they're doing intense physical activity.
sentences.zh: 第二种被称为劳力型热射病，它可能发生在任何人身上，即使是非常健康的人，当他们进行剧烈体力活动时。

sentences.en: It could be a roofer or an athlete working out in the hot sun.
sentences.zh: 可能是屋顶工人，也可能是烈日下锻炼的运动员。

sentences.en: As your body heats up, it reacts automatically, pumping more blood toward the surface of your skin, where it can get cooler as you sweat.
sentences.zh: 当你的身体变热时，它会自动反应，将更多的血液泵向皮肤表面，在那里通过排汗来降温。

sentences.en: That's a normal physical process.
sentences.zh: 这是一个正常的生理过程。

sentences.en: But if it's too hot outside, it starts to break down.
sentences.zh: 但如果室外太热，这个过程就会开始崩溃。

sentences.en: If it's too hot, your blood can't cool off fast enough.
sentences.zh: 如果太热，你的血液就无法足够快地冷却下来。

sentences.en: So what starts to happen is your heart starts pounding faster and faster.
sentences.zh: 于是，你的心脏开始跳得越来越快。

sentences.en: Again, here's Jeff Goodell.
sentences.zh: 再次提到杰夫·古德尔。

sentences.en: Starts to kind of panic and think, OK, I need to cool off.
sentences.zh: 它开始有点恐慌，心想，好吧，我需要降温。

sentences.en: We're not cooling off fast enough.
sentences.zh: 我们降温的速度不够快。

sentences.en: I need to push more blood and more blood.
sentences.zh: 我需要输送更多的血液，更多的血液。

sentences.en: In the case of heat stroke, this can become a runaway process, where your body pulls blood away from your brain and internal organs,
sentences.zh: 在中暑的情况下，这可能变成一个失控的过程，你的身体将血液从大脑和内脏器官中抽离，

sentences.en: desperately pumping it towards your skin to try and cool it down.
sentences.zh: 拼命地将其泵向皮肤以试图降温。

sentences.en: And if you don't start cooling off, then your body temperature starts rising and rising.
sentences.zh: 如果你不开始降温，那么你的体温就会不断升高。

sentences.en: And once it gets above 103 or 104 degrees, which is only 5, 6 degrees above the normal body temperature,
sentences.zh: 一旦超过103或104华氏度，这仅仅比正常体温高出5到6度，

sentences.en: then you start to get into real serious problems where the actual cell membranes in your body,
sentences.zh: 那么你就会遇到非常严重的问题，你体内的细胞膜，

sentences.en: especially in your internal organs, begin to actually melt.
sentences.zh: 尤其是内脏器官中的细胞膜，开始真正融化。

sentences.en: And your body kind of, I know this sounds like a terrible thing to say, but it's true.
sentences.zh: 你的身体有点像——我知道这听起来很可怕，但这是真的。

sentences.en: It kind of liquefies from the inside.
sentences.zh: 它从内部开始液化。

sentences.en: In most ERs, the standard care for heat stroke is something called active cooling.
sentences.zh: 在大多数急诊室，中暑的标准治疗方法被称为主动降温。

sentences.en: That means misting the patient or covering them with a cool, wet sheet and blowing fans on them.
sentences.zh: 这意味着给患者喷雾，或者用凉爽的湿床单覆盖他们，并用风扇吹他们。

sentences.en: But when you're seeing a lot of patients come in with really severe heat stroke, then you start getting creative.
sentences.zh: 但当你看到大量患有严重热射病的患者涌入时，你就得发挥创造力了。

sentences.en: We're one of the only hospitals that does a whole body cold water immersion therapy for all of our heat strokes.
sentences.zh: 我们是为数不多的对所有中暑患者进行全身冷水浸泡治疗的医院之一。

sentences.en: So this is our EMS entrance.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的急救入口。

sentences.en: And as a patient is coming in, especially if they're coming in from like pre-hospital or EMS,
sentences.zh: 当患者被送进来时，特别是如果他们是从院前急救或EMS送来的，

sentences.en: they're going to be coming and wheeling right through here as they're going to our resuscitation rooMs.
sentences.zh: 他们会被直接推过这里，送往我们的复苏室。

sentences.en: Dr. Komp demonstrated what happens when a patient gets rushed in with suspected heat stroke.
sentences.zh: 康普医生演示了当疑似中暑的患者被紧急送入时会发生什么。

sentences.en: What they do is they wheel the patient into a room where they do the first round of resuscitations.
sentences.zh: 他们会把患者推进一个房间，进行第一轮复苏。

sentences.en: And then they place the patient in a giant plastic body bag and pack ice in around them.
sentences.zh: 然后他们把患者放进一个巨大的塑料尸袋里，并在周围塞满冰块。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, I need a better term, but we're just zipping people into body bags, filling it up with ice and water and then zipping them back up.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，我需要一个更好的词，但我们就是把人拉进尸袋，填满冰和水，然后拉上拉链。

sentences.en: But making sure that we're keeping arms and, frankly, the face and airway exposed so we can continue with vital signs and getting IV access,
sentences.zh: 但要确保手臂，坦率地说，还有面部和气道暴露在外，这样我们才能继续监测生命体征并进行静脉通路建立，

sentences.en: but also continuing to monitor our patient status.
sentences.zh: 同时也继续监测患者的状态。

sentences.en: Sometimes if patients are treated fast enough, they recover.
sentences.zh: 有时如果治疗足够及时，患者是可以康复的。

sentences.en: But even people who survive can have organ damage and neurological problems that stay with them.
sentences.zh: 但即使是幸存者也可能留下器官损伤和神经系统问题。

sentences.en: It's sad because this is an absolutely preventable disease.
sentences.zh: 这很可悲，因为这完全是一种可以预防的疾病。

sentences.en: I mean, different people are affected based on different risk factors, different underlying medical problems, other intoxications and drug use.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不同的人受到的影响取决于不同的风险因素、不同的潜在医疗问题、其他中毒和药物使用情况。

sentences.en: But for the most part, if we can get someone out of the heat, we can prevent a lot of death.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，如果我们能让人脱离高温环境，我们就能预防很多死亡。

sentences.en: There's a brutal simplicity to who is most at risk for heat stroke.
sentences.zh: 谁最容易中暑，这背后有着残酷的简单逻辑。

sentences.en: It's the people who have trouble escaping the heat because they don't have air conditioning or it's broken
sentences.zh: 就是那些难以逃避高温的人，因为他们没有空调，或者空调坏了，

sentences.en: or too expensive to run, or they're older and have health issues and live alone.
sentences.zh: 或者运行成本太高，又或者他们年纪大了、有健康问题且独居。

sentences.en: Or they're struggling with addiction and are vulnerable to passing out in the sun.
sentences.zh: 或者他们正在与毒瘾作斗争，容易在烈日下昏倒。

sentences.en: Or they live outside.
sentences.zh: 或者他们露宿街头。

sentences.en: All of which means that vulnerability to heat is tied up with big structural problems that can be hard to solve,
sentences.zh: 所有这些都意味着对高温的脆弱性与难以解决的重大结构性问题紧密相连，

sentences.en: like homelessness, addiction, poverty, and housing.
sentences.zh: 比如无家可归、毒瘾、贫困和住房问题。

sentences.en: Keeping people safe from heat is both easy, just give them a place to cool down, and hard.
sentences.zh: 保护人们免受高温伤害既容易——给他们一个降温的地方——又很难。

sentences.en: Do you currently or have you ever had a case manager helping you towards housing?
sentences.zh: 你目前或曾经有案例经理帮助你解决住房问题吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: I'm back in the Circle K parking lot with Sergio Armandadis.
sentences.zh: 我又回到了Circle K停车场，和塞尔吉奥·阿曼达迪斯在一起。

sentences.en: He's the outreach worker with the Phoenix Rescue Mission.
sentences.zh: 他是菲尼克斯救援任务的外展工作人员。

sentences.en: And now he's chatting up a guy named Jason Joseph, who ticks the boxes for many of the risk factors I just listed.
sentences.zh: 现在他正在和一个叫杰森·约瑟夫的人聊天，这个人符合我刚才列出的许多风险因素。

sentences.en: How has this summer been for you, kind of heat-wise?
sentences.zh: 这个夏天对你来说怎么样，就高温而言？

sentences.en: A couple days were ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 有几天简直荒唐透顶。

sentences.en: I thought I was going to die.
sentences.zh: 我以为自己快要死了。

sentences.en: On one of the hottest days, when temperatures were up near 120,
sentences.zh: 在最热的几天里，气温高达近120华氏度（约49摄氏度），

sentences.en: Jason undertook his own improvised cold water immersion.
sentences.zh: 杰森尝试了他自己临时想出的冷水浸泡法。

sentences.en: He headed over to a nearby ditch, and despite the terrible smell of the water, he jumped in.
sentences.zh: 他走到附近的一条沟渠边，尽管水散发着恶臭，他还是跳了进去。

sentences.en: I was so glad for that.
sentences.zh: 我当时真是太庆幸了。

sentences.en: All I could do is lay in the shade, soaking wet.
sentences.zh: 我唯一能做的就是浑身湿透地躺在阴凉处。

sentences.en: And then it'd get so hot, I had to go back in the ravine and then go back to the shade.
sentences.zh: 然后天气变得太热了，我不得不回到沟壑里，然后再回到阴凉处。

sentences.en: So it's like you just spent the whole day like that.
sentences.zh: 所以就像是你整天都在那样度过。

sentences.en: Just cooling.
sentences.zh: 只是为了降温。

sentences.en: I couldn't do anything else that day.
sentences.zh: 那天我什么也做不了。

sentences.en: I had to just cool.
sentences.zh: 我只能让自己凉快下来。

sentences.en: So the mission was maintaining.
sentences.zh: 所以任务就是维持生存。

sentences.en: Because a lot of the places, you'd think, oh, why don't you just go inside somewhere?
sentences.zh: 因为很多地方，你可能会想，噢，为什么不找个地方进去呢？

sentences.en: But they would kick me out anywhere because I was dirty and, you know, my hair all messed up.
sentences.zh: 但他们会把我赶出来，因为我很脏，而且，你知道，我的头发乱糟糟的。

sentences.en: And they're just like, no, get out of here.
sentences.zh: 他们只会说，不，从这儿滚开。

sentences.en: Jason survived that day, but from talking to him, it sounds like every day in July and August required a kind of desperate improvisation to cool himself down,
sentences.zh: 杰森那天活了下来，但从与他的交谈中听起来，七月和八月的每一天都需要某种绝望的即兴发挥来让自己降温，

sentences.en: one way or another, like stumbling on an air-conditioned church that wouldn't turn him away,
sentences.zh: 以某种方式，比如偶然发现一家不会把他拒之门外的有空调的教堂，

sentences.en: or finding a little piece of shade where a breeze would pass over him.
sentences.zh: 或者找到一小片有微风吹过的地方。

sentences.en: Yeah, there was maybe a little over a month ago.
sentences.zh: 是的，大概是一个多月前吧。

sentences.en: This was on a Sunday.
sentences.zh: 那是周日。

sentences.en: Back in the car with Sergio, you can hear the AC running again.
sentences.zh: 回到塞尔吉奥的车里，你可以听到空调又在运转了。

sentences.en: Normally, as a radio producer, I would ask the person I'm talking with to turn it off so that I could record their voice more clearly.
sentences.zh: 通常作为一名广播制作人，我会要求交谈对象关掉空调，以便我能更清晰地录下他们的声音。

sentences.en: But there is no way I'm doing that in Phoenix.
sentences.zh: 但在菲尼克斯，我绝不可能那样做。

sentences.en: And as we drive on to a new location, Sergio tells me about an experience he had recently.
sentences.zh: 当我们开车前往下一个地点时，塞尔吉奥告诉我他最近的一次经历。

sentences.en: He was sitting in a park.
sentences.zh: 他当时坐在公园里。

sentences.en: And I'm sitting there, and I see that there's police, and it looks like a body on the ground.
sentences.zh: 我坐在那儿，看到有警察，地上好像躺着一具尸体。

sentences.en: And so I'm just kind of wondering, like, is that a body?
sentences.zh: 所以我当时就在想，那是尸体吗？

sentences.en: I can't tell.
sentences.zh: 我看不出来。

sentences.en: Eventually, the police strung yellow tape around the figure.
sentences.zh: 最终，警察在那个身影周围拉起了黄色警戒线。

sentences.en: And then I realized it is a body, and I just couldn't help but wonder about that person, you know?
sentences.zh: 然后我意识到那确实是一具尸体，我忍不住开始为那个人感到好奇，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Like, how did they die?
sentences.zh: 比如，他们是怎么死的？

sentences.en: Was it the heat?
sentences.zh: 是因为高温吗？

sentences.en: Was it drugs?
sentences.zh: 是因为毒品吗？

sentences.en: Was it a mixture?
sentences.zh: 还是两者都有？

sentences.en: The questions that Sergio is asking, how did they die?
sentences.zh: 塞尔吉奥提出的这些问题，他们是怎么死的？

sentences.en: Was it the heat?
sentences.zh: 是因为高温吗？

sentences.en: Was it drugs?
sentences.zh: 是因为毒品吗？

sentences.en: It turns out there's a person whose job it is to find the answers.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，有一个人的工作就是寻找这些答案。

sentences.en: So I'm Dr. Jeff Johnston.
sentences.zh: 我是杰夫·约翰斯顿医生。

sentences.en: I'm the chief medical examiner for Maricopa County.
sentences.zh: 我是马里科帕县的首席法医。

sentences.en: As the chief medical examiner, Dr. Johnston oversees a staff of 120 people.
sentences.zh: 作为首席法医，约翰斯顿医生管理着一个120人的团队。

sentences.en: They're responsible for investigating the non-natural deaths that happen in the county,
sentences.zh: 他们负责调查该县发生的非自然死亡事件，

sentences.en: including the ones where heat might be a factor.
sentences.zh: 包括那些高温可能是诱因的死亡事件。

sentences.en: Dr. Johnston speaks with a disarming directness about his work.
sentences.zh: 约翰斯顿医生在谈论他的工作时，有着一种令人卸下防备的直率。

sentences.en: And the way he referred to the summer months will probably stay with me forever.
sentences.zh: 他形容夏季月份的方式可能会让我终生难忘。

sentences.en: Really, we do look at this like a mass fatality event.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我们确实把这看作是一起大规模伤亡事件。

sentences.en: A mass fatality event.
sentences.zh: 大规模伤亡事件。

sentences.en: It's a phrase I associate with shootings or acts of terrorism.
sentences.zh: 这是一个我通常与枪击案或恐怖袭击联系在一起的词汇。

sentences.en: But he's just talking about June, July, and AuguSt.
sentences.zh: 但他指的仅仅是六月、七月和八月。

sentences.en: Where you have a sudden surge in the number of deaths that you've got to investigate that outstrip your typical resources.
sentences.zh: 那时死亡人数会突然激增，你必须进行调查，这超出了你通常的资源承受能力。

sentences.en: Figuring out whether a person died from heat-related causes is actually harder than you might think.
sentences.zh: 弄清楚一个人是否死于高温相关原因，实际上比你想象的要难。

sentences.en: Despite its devastating effects on the body, heat stroke doesn't really have a specific physical signature that shows up in an autopsy.
sentences.zh: 尽管高温对身体有毁灭性的影响，但中暑在尸检中并没有真正具体的物理特征。

sentences.en: Heat-induced death looks a lot like organ failure or just general decay.
sentences.zh: 高温导致的死亡看起来很像器官衰竭或一般的身体腐烂。

sentences.en: And so, understanding the context in which the body was found is key.
sentences.zh: 因此，了解发现尸体时的环境背景是关键。

sentences.en: To do that, the department employs 40 medical legal death investigators.
sentences.zh: 为了做到这一点，该部门雇佣了40名法医死亡调查员。

sentences.en: They go out to scenes to collect information.
sentences.zh: 他们会前往现场收集信息。

sentences.en: Whether air conditioner's working, whether they've got access to food, water,
sentences.zh: 比如空调是否在工作，他们是否能获得食物、水，

sentences.en: collecting information at the scene, those temperatures,
sentences.zh: 在现场收集信息，那些温度数据，

sentences.en: other signs of risk factors that help our forensic pathologists to make the correct conclusion about what caused or contributed to the death.
sentences.zh: 以及其他风险因素的迹象，这些都有助于我们的法医病理学家对死亡原因或促成因素做出正确的结论。

sentences.en: Last summer, the scenes that Johnston's team of investigators encountered were difficult.
sentences.zh: 去年夏天，约翰斯顿的调查员团队所面对的现场情况非常艰难。

sentences.en: They found bodies curled up in tents, stretched out on the asphalt, slumped in backyards,
sentences.zh: 他们发现尸体蜷缩在帐篷里，横躺在沥青路面上，瘫倒在后院里，

sentences.en: or entombed in houses where the air conditioning had broken and the temperatures inside had soared to 130 degrees.
sentences.zh: 或者被困在空调坏掉的房子里，室内温度飙升到了130华氏度（约54摄氏度）。

sentences.en: Everyone was stretched to capacity.
sentences.zh: 每个人都已达到极限。

sentences.en: The office was dealing with so many bodies that they had to call in for extra refrigerated trailers for backup storage.
sentences.zh: 办公室处理的尸体太多，以至于不得不要求提供额外的冷藏拖车作为备用存储。

sentences.en: And they would have brought in more pathologists, but there weren't any.
sentences.zh: 他们本想引入更多的病理学家，但根本没有。

sentences.en: It doesn't seem like an easy job to just staff up.
sentences.zh: 增加人手似乎并不是一件容易的事。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: Your skills are so specialized, there's probably not just a bunch of, like, temp medical examiners hanging around Phoenix.
sentences.zh: 你的技能非常专业，菲尼克斯可能没有一大堆临时法医闲着没事干。

sentences.en: Definitely, yeah.
sentences.zh: 确实，是的。

sentences.en: If we have a vacancy, it's on average 20 months for us to be able to fill it.
sentences.zh: 如果我们有空缺，平均需要20个月才能填补。

sentences.en: All offices across the country are really struggling with that and have been for the better part of two decades.
sentences.zh: 全国各地的办公室都在为此苦苦挣扎，这种情况已经持续了近二十年。

sentences.en: So, you can add pathologists to the list of our already overburdened infrastructure buckling under the weight of climate change.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以把病理学家加入到我们那本已不堪重负、在气候变化重压下摇摇欲坠的基础设施名单中。

sentences.en: Our housing is inadequate.
sentences.zh: 我们的住房条件不足。

sentences.en: Our insurance systems aren't ready.
sentences.zh: 我们的保险系统还没准备好。

sentences.en: Our roads and bridges and levees are aging and flimsy.
sentences.zh: 我们的道路、桥梁和堤坝正在老化且脆弱不堪。

sentences.en: And our medical examiners are very, very tired.
sentences.zh: 而我们的法医们也非常、非常疲惫。

sentences.en: In Phoenix, it increasingly appears to be a predictable annual disaster.
sentences.zh: 在菲尼克斯，这似乎正日益成为一场可预测的年度灾难。

sentences.en: But, amazingly, that's not the way the federal government sees it.
sentences.zh: 但令人惊讶的是，联邦政府并不是这样看待它的。

sentences.en: Extreme heat is not on the list of disasters that FEMA is authorized to respond to.
sentences.zh: 极端高温并不在联邦紧急事务管理局（FEMA）授权应对的灾难名单上。

sentences.en: There's been a vast underestimation of the risks of heat and the dangers of heat.
sentences.zh: 人们对高温的风险和危险存在巨大的低估。

sentences.en: That even the people at FEMA are still behind the curve in recalculating the risks of this new climate world that we're living in.
sentences.zh: 甚至连FEMA的人在重新评估我们所处这个新气候世界的风险方面也依然滞后。

sentences.en: And that's partly because so many of heat's victims are still unseen.
sentences.zh: 这部分是因为许多高温受害者仍然不被看见。

sentences.en: The data on heat-related deaths across the country and around the world remains inadequate.
sentences.zh: 全国乃至全世界关于高温相关死亡的数据仍然不足。

sentences.en: And heat kills a lot of people who are living on the margins.
sentences.zh: 而且高温夺去了许多生活在社会边缘的人的生命。

sentences.en: They're not the people that are out there lobbying for more protection.
sentences.zh: 他们不是那些在外面游说要求更多保护的人。

sentences.en: But it's also because of the fundamental way that our government thinks about disasters.
sentences.zh: 但这同样是因为我们政府看待灾难的根本方式。

sentences.en: It's geared towards damage to stuff rather than damage to people.
sentences.zh: 它更倾向于关注物质损失，而不是人员损失。

sentences.en: The government overwhelmingly uses property value as a metric when weighing how to dish out funds after disasters happen.
sentences.zh: 政府在权衡灾后如何分配资金时，绝大多数情况下使用财产价值作为衡量标准。

sentences.en: And in some ways, that calculation makes sense.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，这种计算是有道理的。

sentences.en: It's hard and time-consuming to investigate heat-related deaths.
sentences.zh: 调查高温相关死亡事件既困难又耗时。

sentences.en: And it's hard to quantify damage when you're talking about overstretched social workers.
sentences.zh: 而且当你谈论超负荷工作的社会工作者时，很难量化损失。

sentences.en: Or a hospital system struggling to keep up with its patient load.
sentences.zh: 或者一个正在努力应对病人负担的医院系统。

sentences.en: Or what's lost when a person needlessly dies on a hot sidewalk.
sentences.zh: 又或者当一个人在炎热的人行道上无谓地死去时，究竟失去了什么。

sentences.en: But that means that places like Phoenix, and hot places across the country, are largely left to fend for themselves every summer.
sentences.zh: 但这确实意味着像菲尼克斯这样的地方，以及全国各地的炎热地区，每年夏天基本上只能自生自灭。

sentences.en: When heat is extracting a terrible human toll.
sentences.zh: 而高温正在造成可怕的人员伤亡。

sentences.en: Jeff Goodell sometimes calls air conditioning a technology of forgetting.
sentences.zh: 杰夫·古德尔有时称空调为“遗忘的技术”。

sentences.en: The ability to cool ourselves down obscures the fact that the world around us is getting much hotter and more dangerous.
sentences.zh: 我们让自己凉快下来的能力掩盖了一个事实，那就是我们周围的世界正变得越来越热、越来越危险。

sentences.en: Even Sergio Armandadiz, who lived on the streets of Phoenix for five years, sometimes forgets what that experience was like.
sentences.zh: 即使是已经在菲尼克斯街头生活了五年的塞尔吉奥·阿曼达迪兹，有时也会忘记那段经历是什么样的。

sentences.en: He and his wife, who was also homeless, will joke about how soft they've gotten.
sentences.zh: 他和同样曾无家可归的妻子会开玩笑说他们变得多么娇气。

sentences.en: How they complain when the AC can't get their house any cooler on the hottest summer days.
sentences.zh: 抱怨在最热的夏日里空调无法让房子更凉快一些。

sentences.en: So I'm like, what happened to us?
sentences.zh: 所以我说，我们怎么了？

sentences.en: We used to be gangster out there just dealing with it like nothing.
sentences.zh: 我们以前在外面像个硬汉一样，什么都不在乎地应对着。

sentences.en: And now we're just complaining about 75 degree AC.
sentences.zh: 而现在我们却在抱怨75华氏度（约24摄氏度）的空调。

sentences.en: It's like, jeez.
sentences.zh: 真是的，天哪。

sentences.en: There's a question hovering in the background of this whole story.
sentences.zh: 在这个故事的背景中一直萦绕着一个问题。

sentences.en: Will Phoenix be a livable place in another 20 or 50 or 100 years?
sentences.zh: 再过20年、50年或100年，菲尼克斯还会是一个适宜居住的地方吗？

sentences.en: This was a question I posed a few times in interviews.
sentences.zh: 这是我在采访中几次提出的问题。

sentences.en: And most people did not appreciate being asked about it.
sentences.zh: 大多数人并不喜欢被问到这个问题。

sentences.en: People will continue living in Phoenix for a lot of good reasons, like jobs and housing and family.
sentences.zh: 人们会因为许多充分的理由继续住在菲尼克斯，比如工作、住房和家庭。

sentences.en: But it's also true that in a typical year, back in the early 90s, Phoenix experienced about seven days above 110 degrees annually.
sentences.zh: 但同样真实的是，在90年代初的典型年份里，菲尼克斯每年大约有七天气温超过110华氏度（约43摄氏度）。

sentences.en: Last year, in 2023, by the time all the days were tallied, the city saw 55 days at those temperatures.
sentences.zh: 去年，即2023年，当所有天数统计完毕时，这座城市经历了55天这样的高温。

sentences.en: And yes, Phoenix is doing a lot of important adaptation work right now.
sentences.zh: 是的，菲尼克斯目前正在做许多重要的适应性工作。

sentences.en: The city created the first publicly funded heat response office in the whole country.
sentences.zh: 该市建立了全国第一个由公共资助的高温响应办公室。

sentences.en: They're building new air-conditioned homeless shelters out of shipping containers.
sentences.zh: 他们正在用集装箱建造新的有空调的无家可归者收容所。

sentences.en: And preparation for summer happens year-round.
sentences.zh: 而且夏季的准备工作全年都在进行。

sentences.en: But there are limits to our ability to adapt.
sentences.zh: 但我们的适应能力是有极限的。

sentences.en: We don't know exactly where those limits are.
sentences.zh: 我们并不确切知道这些极限在哪里。

sentences.en: We don't know exactly when we'll hit them.
sentences.zh: 我们并不确切知道什么时候会触及这些极限。

sentences.en: It depends a lot on what you're willing to endure.
sentences.zh: 这很大程度上取决于你愿意忍受什么。

sentences.en: With enough money and enough technology, you could live on Mars, right?
sentences.zh: 只要有足够的钱和技术，你甚至可以在火星上生活，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, you can live that way.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以那样生活。

sentences.en: But do you want to live in a place where when you go outside, you can't touch the steering wheel on your car?
sentences.zh: 但你想住在一个当你走到外面时，连车上的方向盘都摸不得的地方吗？

sentences.en: If you fall on the sidewalk, you get third-degree burns.
sentences.zh: 如果你摔倒在人行道上，会受到三度烧伤。

sentences.en: Where animals are dying because it's so hot.
sentences.zh: 动物因为太热而死去的地方。

sentences.en: Where people on the street are literally dying on the streets because it is so hot.
sentences.zh: 街上的人因为太热而真的死在街头的地方。

sentences.en: I mean, is that the kind of world you want to live in?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是你想居住的世界吗？

sentences.en: Not me.
sentences.zh: 我不想。

sentences.en: I'd move.
sentences.zh: 我会搬走。

sentences.en: But in the meantime, people are arriving in Phoenix, not leaving.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，人们正在涌入菲尼克斯，而不是离开。

sentences.en: It's still one of the fastest-growing cities in the whole country.
sentences.zh: 它仍然是全国增长最快的城市之一。

sentences.en: For at least six months a year, the weather is still glorious.
sentences.zh: 一年中至少有六个月，天气依然美妙无比。

sentences.en: People still want to live in the land without winter.
sentences.zh: 人们仍然想住在没有冬天的土地上。

sentences.en: And at least for now, many are finding ways to make it work.
sentences.zh: 至少目前，许多人正在找到让生活继续下去的方法。

sentences.en: The people I spoke with in Phoenix were like messengers from the future,
sentences.zh: 我在菲尼克斯交谈过的人就像来自未来的信使，

sentences.en: spelling out a vision of what our hotter world might look like.
sentences.zh: 阐述了我们这个更炎热的世界可能是什么样子的愿景。

sentences.en: And that hotter world looks nocturnal.
sentences.zh: 而那个更炎热的世界看起来是夜行性的。

sentences.en: Everywhere in the summer, people shift their lives towards the early morning and late evening,
sentences.zh: 夏天到处都是，人们把生活重心转移到清晨和深夜，

sentences.en: when temperatures are cooler.
sentences.zh: 那时气温比较凉爽。

sentences.en: People hike at night with headlamps.
sentences.zh: 人们戴着头灯在晚上徒步旅行。

sentences.en: The zoo opens at 6 a.m.
sentences.zh: 动物园早上6点开门，

sentences.en: so that kids can enjoy it before the real heat kicks in and all the animals hide.
sentences.zh: 这样孩子们可以在真正的酷暑到来、所有动物都躲起来之前享受游园。

sentences.en: And from April to September, there are a series of trail races called the Insomniac Night Runs,
sentences.zh: 从四月到九月，有一系列名为“失眠者夜跑”的越野赛，

sentences.en: which start in the evening and continue through the night on desert trails surrounding the city.
sentences.zh: 它们在傍晚开始，整夜在城市周围的沙漠小径上进行。

sentences.en: Last finishers coming through.
sentences.zh: 最后几名选手正在冲线。

sentences.en: It's a real scene, with music and beer served at the finish line,
sentences.zh: 那真是一个热闹的场面，终点线有音乐和啤酒供应，

sentences.en: and runners high-fiving their friends.
sentences.zh: 跑者们与朋友击掌庆祝。

sentences.en: Let's give these guys a big round of applause.
sentences.zh: 让我们为这些人热烈鼓掌。

sentences.en: This particular race is happening at the McDowell Mountain Regional Park,
sentences.zh: 这场特别的比赛是在麦克道尔山地区公园举行的，

sentences.en: about 45 minutes from downtown Phoenix.
sentences.zh: 距离菲尼克斯市中心大约45分钟路程。

sentences.en: The trail winds through a Sonoran desert landscape, and it's gorgeous here.
sentences.zh: 这条小径蜿蜒穿过索诺兰沙漠的景观，这里美极了。

sentences.en: I can imagine the runners racing under the stars, past prickly pears and saguaros,
sentences.zh: 我可以想象跑者们在星空下奔跑，经过仙人掌和巨人柱，

sentences.en: some of them wilting from the heat.
sentences.zh: 其中一些人正因酷热而萎靡不振。

sentences.en: I imagine that even in the dark, the runners are guzzling water
sentences.zh: 我想即使在黑暗中，跑者们也在大口喝水，

sentences.en: and stuffing ice in their shirts and shorts to keep cool.
sentences.zh: 往衬衫和短裤里塞冰块来降温。

sentences.en: They're finding ways to keep doing this thing they love, in a place they love,
sentences.zh: 他们正在寻找方法，在自己热爱的地方，继续做着他们热爱的事情，

sentences.en: despite the immense challenge of it.
sentences.zh: 尽管这面临着巨大的挑战。

sentences.en: Trying to get their miles in before the sun rises and a new, even hotter day begins.
sentences.zh: 试图在太阳升起、新的一天变得更加炎热之前完成他们的里程。

sentences.en: The thing about the big story of climate change is that we're only in the first chapter.
sentences.zh: 关于气候变化这个宏大叙事，关键在于我们目前只处于第一章。

sentences.en: Here's Emmett again.
sentences.zh: 埃米特又来了。

sentences.en: We're only just starting to feel the magnitude of the changes we've unleashed
sentences.zh: 我们才刚刚开始感受到我们所引发的变化的严重性，

sentences.en: and how they will cascade into nearly every aspect of our lives.
sentences.zh: 以及这些变化将如何波及我们生活的几乎方方面面。

sentences.en: For some people, climate change has already been disastrous.
sentences.zh: 对一些人来说，气候变化已经造成了灾难。

sentences.en: It has destroyed homes and uprooted lives.
sentences.zh: 它摧毁了家园，让人们流离失所。

sentences.en: For others, the changes have been subtler.
sentences.zh: 对另一些人来说，这些变化则更为细微。

sentences.en: But the signs are all there, lurking in our rearranged running schedules
sentences.zh: 但迹象无处不在，潜伏在我们调整后的跑步计划中，

sentences.en: and our insurance statements and our air conditioning bills.
sentences.zh: 潜伏在我们的保险单和空调账单里。

sentences.en: This isn't the apocalypse, just a series of unravelings.
sentences.zh: 这并非世界末日，只是一系列解体过程。

sentences.en: And while we're all busy worrying about the end of the world,
sentences.zh: 当我们忙于担心世界末日时，

sentences.en: the world is just changing beneath our feet and leaving us behind.
sentences.zh: 世界正在我们脚下悄然改变，并将我们抛在身后。

sentences.en: There's a lot that we can do to try and catch up.
sentences.zh: 我们能做很多事情来尝试追赶。

sentences.en: We can run at night and replace our wooden floorboards.
sentences.zh: 我们可以夜跑，可以更换木地板。

sentences.en: We can keep people cool and give the river more room to meander.
sentences.zh: 我们可以让人们保持凉爽，给河流留出更多的蜿蜒空间。

sentences.en: And unlike a cactus, we can move out of harm's way.
sentences.zh: 而且与仙人掌不同，我们可以搬离危险地带。

sentences.en: None of that will be easy.
sentences.zh: 这一切都不会容易。

sentences.en: And when you do a lot of stories about adapting to climate change,
sentences.zh: 当你做了很多关于适应气候变化的报道后，

sentences.en: you can't help but come away feeling like we need to do everything in our power
sentences.zh: 你难免会觉得，我们必须竭尽全力，

sentences.en: not to make this hard job harder on ourselves.
sentences.zh: 不要让这项艰巨的工作变得更加困难。

sentences.en: We need to stop the forces that are irrevocably changing our planet.
sentences.zh: 我们需要阻止那些正在不可逆转地改变我们星球的力量。

sentences.en: And at the same time, be honest about the degree to which our planet has already been changed.
sentences.zh: 同时，也要坦诚面对我们的星球已经被改变的程度。

sentences.en: When I'm feeling anxious about the uncertainty of the world right now, which is often,
sentences.zh: 当我因为当今世界的各种不确定性而感到焦虑时——这种情况经常发生——

sentences.en: I find myself yearning for a feeling of stability that I really only felt during my own childhood.
sentences.zh: 我发现自己渴望一种稳定性，那种我只在童年时期感受过的稳定性。

sentences.en: Living my quaint little life in my quaint little Vermont town.
sentences.zh: 过着我那古朴小镇里古朴的小生活。

sentences.en: I find myself wanting to go back there to a mild July day,
sentences.zh: 我发现自己想回到那里，回到一个温和的七月天，

sentences.en: skipping rocks in the gentle flow of the Winooski,
sentences.zh: 在温努斯基河平缓的流水中打水漂，

sentences.en: or curled up with a novel in the back of the creaky old bookstore.
sentences.zh: 或者蜷缩在吱呀作响的老书店后面读小说。

sentences.en: That river still exists.
sentences.zh: 那条河依然存在。

sentences.en: And that bookstore still exists.
sentences.zh: 那家书店也依然存在。

sentences.en: But they're in a different world now.
sentences.zh: 但它们现在处于一个不同的世界里。

sentences.en: We all are.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都是如此。

sentences.en: And the task ahead is to embrace the hard work of living in the world as it is.
sentences.zh: 而摆在我们面前的任务，是拥抱在当今世界中生活的艰辛。
